newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain could save 130 bln pta in interest in '97.
newsitem.headline: Spain could save 130 bln pta in interest in '97.

text.p: Spain, already benefitting from a sharp reduction in long-term interest rates, could save another 130 billion pesetas in interest expenditures in the 1997 budget.

"There are significant savings for the budget. The amount could be 130 billion pesetas if interest rates remain where they are now until the end of 1997," Jaime Caruana, general director of the Spanish Treasury, told Reuters in an interview.
The interview will be broadcast later on Reuters Financial Television.

"We made the interest rate expenditure forecast (in the budget), which is 3.46 trillion pesetas, based on the yield curve at that time. Since then there has been significant reductions (in yields)," Caruana said.
Caruana added that every full point fall in interest rates represents a savings of 400 billion pesetas, but the full effect is only felt after a few years.
He said that the reduction in market interest rates Spain had experienced this year, to seven percent from 10 percent, should bear full fruits in the coming years.
